races.name: Seadell Shops & Holiday Chalets 'Hands And Heels' Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Pleasant Man
runners_data.note: Showed a placed effort over 12f on good ground most recently and arrives fresh on 12 days' rest; the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that his OR-70 profile places him in a front-running or prominent role that is slightly out of character at this longer trip, but with no challengers for the lead his tactical advantage is real and should not be dismissed lightly.
runners_data.comment: Won a handicap at Doncaster 12 days ago, scoring by 1¼l off a 3lb lower mark in a performance that underlines his current solid form; effective across 10-14f and first-time cheekpieces are an interesting addition — he heads the ratings with a strong case.

runners_data.name: Hibernate
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's four-year-old carries strong recent form — two wins including a 12f success on firm and a runner-up on good — and a trainer 14-day strike rate of 3/13 adds confidence; Toby Moore takes over in the saddle, and 36 days since last run should not inconvenience a horse who has been clearly produced fresh before.
runners_data.comment: Won by four lengths off a 6lb lower mark at his penultimate start and clearly suited by distances from 9f to 12f; his most recent run was well below that level off the same mark he carries today, but the ground and trip suit and there may still be improvement in him.

runners_data.name: Currumbin
runners_data.note: Michael Keady's five-year-old has been off 82 days, which is the longest break in this field, and his recent form reading of 8663-0 at distances stretching to 16f raises fitness and confidence concerns; a hold-up style requires the race to truly come apart in front, and on a flat Yarmouth straight with a single loose leader that is an optimistic ask.
runners_data.comment: Out of form on his most recent start here on the Flat and has proven most effective over longer distances of 12f to 16f, making today's shorter trip an obvious concern; a first-time hood is fitted after a break of 82 days and he has plenty to find against these rivals.

runners_data.name: The Ubermensch
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's consistent four-year-old has placed six times in recent starts and returns on just six days' rest suggesting good current form; fitted with a tongue-tie and carrying 130lbs as the lowest weight in the race, his hold-up style means he needs something to go wrong in front, but his consistency makes him the more trustworthy of the two closers if the race does open up.
runners_data.comment: Just touched off by 1¼l at Newcastle last time off the same mark he carries today, and has been placing consistently across 8-12f on good-to-firm and AW surfaces; tongue-tie and cheekpieces fitted together for the first time suggest connections expect a step forward and he could go close.

races.paceDynamic: Pleasant Man is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of four and will stride into the lead unchallenged from the outset, setting what should be a sustainable, unhurried gallop over this 1m3½f trip on good-to-firm ground at Yarmouth. With no other genuine pace horse to apply pressure, Pleasant Man can dictate every yard and control the tempo entirely to his own liking, which historically favours front-runners who get soft lead fractions. The two hold-up horses, Currumbin and The Ubermensch, will need a meaningful pace injection in the closing stages to generate the momentum to overhaul a loose leader, and on a flat, galloping track like Yarmouth where there is no downhill run to aid hold-up types, that ask is a significant one. This race shape heavily favours horses who can race prominently or sit just off the pace — Hibernate, the only other prominent-style runner, is best placed to track and challenge, while the hold-up horses face the most demanding tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls All
scenarios.trigger: If Pleasant Man dictates a steady-to-moderate tempo throughout without any pressure, stamina and concentration of the front-runner become decisive.
scenarios.body: If Pleasant Man dictates a steady-to-moderate tempo throughout without any pressure, stamina and concentration of the front-runner become decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hibernate Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Hibernate sits a length or two off Pleasant Man and produces a smooth move two furlongs out before the leader can quicken away.
scenarios.body: If Hibernate sits a length or two off Pleasant Man and produces a smooth move two furlongs out before the leader can quicken away.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is just brisk enough to tie up the front two in the final furlong, allowing hold-up horses to close from behind.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is just brisk enough to tie up the front two in the final furlong, allowing hold-up horses to close from behind.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, Any Order
scenarios.trigger: If all four runners are covered by two lengths turning in and a sprint finish unfolds between them.
scenarios.body: If all four runners are covered by two lengths turning in and a sprint finish unfolds between them.

watchPoints.text: Pleasant Man could be very difficult to catch if Toby Moore on Hibernate misjudges the gap and leaves it too late to close — monitor how much daylight Pleasant Man has at the two-furlong pole.

Currumbin's 82-day absence combined with his deteriorating form figures is a significant negative; if he struggles for early momentum from a hold-up position, he could become irrelevant before halfway.

The Ubermensch ran only six days ago — watch for signs of freshness or fatigue in the preliminaries, as back-to-back quick returns can cut both ways for a hold-up horse who needs to produce a sustained late run.

With only four runners and a single pace-setter, any early incident or stumble involving Pleasant Man would completely reshape this race — the lack of an alternative natural leader means Hibernate would be forced to take up the running in a role that suits it better than either closer.

runners_data.name: Can't Stop
runners_data.comment: A 75,000gns Ardad colt on debut, he is a full-brother to Farough, who showed very useful ability at six furlongs, and his dam was smart at the same trip as a juvenile; his trainer is in good form and he has every reason to be considered seriously.

runners_data.name: Nabati
runners_data.comment: Night Of Thunder colt who cost 850,000gns on debut, a half-brother to Chicago Call, who has shown very smart form at six furlongs, with his dam also sharp at that trip; a top course jockey takes the ride and his price tag alone suggests he is a colt of considerable ability.

runners_data.name: Shoof
runners_data.comment: Well held over nine lengths on his debut at Goodwood, but he should do better and today's extra distance may be what he has been waiting for; a hood goes on for the first time and he heads the ratings here, giving connections reason for greater optimism second time out.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Dawn
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a novice on his only start, but that run suggested the trip may not have suited and there is scope to improve with experience; he handles today's course and going and has everything to gain on his second outing if he can build on that debut effort.

races.name: Weatherbys Racing Bank Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Musical Times
runners_data.comment: Landed a novice at Newmarket on debut with a narrow margin and showed enough to suggest she can back it up on her second start; a top course jockey takes the ride and she heads the ratings as the clear one to beat.

runners_data.name: Attack Attack
runners_data.comment: Beaten 7½l in a maiden on this course last time and yet to win in recent starts, but steps up in trip for the first time today which could prove the key; a hood fits for the first time and her trainer is in good form.

runners_data.name: Aunty Patsy
runners_data.comment: An 85,000gns St Mark's Basilica filly on debut, she is a half-sister to Royal Scimitar, who showed smart form at a mile, giving her an attractive pedigree profile for this trip; lightly exposed and holds obvious appeal on paper.

runners_data.name: Gracious Gift
runners_data.comment: A Dubawi filly on debut for a top stable, she is a half-sister to Arabian Light, who showed very smart form at a mile and a quarter, with her dam also sharp at seven furlongs; strong on pedigree and commands real respect here.

runners_data.name: Skyglow
runners_data.comment: A Space Blues filly on debut, she is a half-sister to smart-at-7f Wetsand and her dam showed fair two-year-old ability at a mile; our figures place her at the foot of the field and she has the most to prove in this company, though pedigree is not without appeal.

races.name: Winning Experience With Moulton Racing Handicap

runners_data.name: Great Mates
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed pace-setter who has won at 8f on Standard ground and has course-relevant form; Good to Firm conditions suit and the uncontested lead is a significant asset, though a style-fit tag (0.90) tempers confidence slightly given recent patterns just off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Well held in a handicap at Newmarket last time, though that run was in keeping with her previous effort, and she had been building a solid record beforehand, including a win in recent starts; effective at 8-9f on good ground and AW, with a first-time hood added today.

runners_data.name: Sir Edward Lear
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist dropping sharply back in trip from 10-16f starts to a flat mile; the distance reduction is a concern, but previous good-ground form is solid and Mason Paetel's claim gives a weight advantage if the race develops with a decent gallop.
runners_data.comment: Fourth and beaten seven lengths at Ripon on his latest start, in line with his previous effort, and has scope to build on his flat-season reappearance runs; switched to a visor today and, while his best form has come over 10-12f, there is ability here if he can translate it over a mile.

runners_data.name: Kalamunda
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer who fits this race shape well, with recent second at 8f on Good ground matching today's conditions; trainer Joseph Parr has a quiet 14-day strike rate (0/5) but the horse's positional profile and course-appropriate distance are the key positives here.
runners_data.comment: Posted a clear career-best when runner-up here over course and distance last time, going down by just 2¼l off this same mark; cheekpieces fitted for the first time today and, though his best form has come on AW, he heads the ratings with a strong case to make on recent evidence.

runners_data.name: Tactical Plan
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's hold-up type has hit the frame at 8f on Good ground but also has a string of low finishes; headgear (p) worn, 23 days since last run, and the pattern of finishing mid-pack on quick ground suggests this shape doesn't ideally suit.
runners_data.comment: A slight improvement when fourth at Brighton last time, beaten just over 4 lengths in a handicap, though yet to win in recent starts; acts well on any ground and has form at 7f, while first-time cheekpieces today are an addition that could spark further progress.

runners_data.name: Man Of Desert
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride on a genuine off-the-pace horse that, due to hold-up congestion in the field, has been placed on the map in midfield rather than at his natural position at the rear; the horse's good-ground record at 8f shows limited progress (0W1P) and the compromised running position diminishes his chance.
runners_data.comment: Fourth and beaten 6½l in a handicap on this course most recently, in keeping with his recent form, though the mark has been easing without a win to show for it; a tongue-tie fits for the first time today and the mile trip and sound surface both suit.

runners_data.name: Big Alex Walmsley
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type who has never won or placed in six similar-going runs; pushed into a midfield position on the map because the field is heavy with closers, meaning his typical late-run route is boxed in before the race even starts, and a 0/1 trainer 14-day figure adds no confidence.
runners_data.comment: Well adrift of the principals in a handicap at Lingfield last time, struggling to match his better efforts, and his rating continues to fall without a win in recent starts; a hood is added today and he has fair form at 7f on a sound surface, but sits at the foot of our ratings.

races.paceDynamic: Great Mates is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-horse field and, with no genuine pressure expected from rivals, should dictate a controlled, honest gallop on the Good to Firm Yarmouth mile. Kalamunda will attempt to race prominently alongside or just behind Great Mates, giving the race a two-horse front group, while the remainder — Sir Edward Lear, Tactical Plan, Man Of Desert, and Big Alex Walmsley — will settle in the chasing pack. Note that the field holds more hold-up types than can all occupy the rear: Man Of Desert and Big Alex Walmsley are genuine off-the-pace horses who have been mapped to midfield given the congestion, meaning they are unlikely to find as clean a run late as their natural style would suggest. With a single uncontested pace-setter able to control tempo and conserve energy through the first half of the mile, this race shape strongly favours the prominent racer who can travel close to the early pace and pick up when the tempo lifts in the final two furlongs — a true hold-up finish is made harder by the compressed field and the fact that the truest closers are compromised in their ability to find clear daylight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Great Mates or Kalamunda dictates a steady-honest gallop and the race develops into a sustained two-furlong duel from the front.
scenarios.body: If Great Mates or Kalamunda dictates a steady-honest gallop and the race develops into a sustained two-furlong duel from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Great Mates goes too fast early on the quick ground and ties up inside the final furlong, gifting ground to those held up.
scenarios.body: If Great Mates goes too fast early on the quick ground and ties up inside the final furlong, gifting ground to those held up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If Man Of Desert or Big Alex Walmsley successfully navigate a clear passage from the rear and the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late run.
scenarios.body: If Man Of Desert or Big Alex Walmsley successfully navigate a clear passage from the rear and the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled, Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If Great Mates is restrained or the pace becomes stop-start, turning the race into a sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: If Great Mates is restrained or the pace becomes stop-start, turning the race into a sprint from two furlongs out.

watchPoints.text: Great Mates — watch whether Jack Mitchell (Kalamunda) challenges for the lead early; if he pushes Great Mates into a contested gallop rather than a controlled one, the pace dynamic shifts and the race opens up for the hold-up types.

Man Of Desert and Big Alex Walmsley — both are genuine hold-up horses compressed into midfield; watch at the half-mile pole whether De Sousa and Keenan can find racing room, as a traffic-bound effort from either will confirm the redistribution penalty applies in real time.

Sir Edward Lear — dropping from 10-16f trips to a flat mile is a significant pattern break; watch in the final furlong whether the trip blunts his finish, which would be a key form guide for future outings regardless of today's result.

Kalamunda — the 0/5 trainer 14-day stat is a mild flag, but Jack Mitchell is a strong course-form jockey at Yarmouth; watch whether he tracks Great Mates or gives him daylight, as that positional choice will shape the entire race.

races.name: Mark Sumner Handicap

runners_data.name: Give Me The Night
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type for Mark Rimell with a tongue-tie, finding Good-ground form on similar going (2/9 sim-going, 1P) though has failed to fire recently with a form string of 78-480; Mikey Sheehy rides and 29 days since last run is fine, but needs the sprint finish this race is likely to produce to be competitive.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in recent starts, he is effective at this distance on good and soft, and the addition of first-time blinkers for a trainer in good form makes him of interest from stall 4. A poor run at Nottingham last time is the main question.

runners_data.name: Midnight's Dream
runners_data.note: Joseph Parr's five-year-old carries modest recent form (390006) and a poor record on similar going (1W2P from 15 runs), but Jack Mitchell is a quality booking and the horse's natural closing style suits the bunched-sprint shape this race is set to produce; 18 days since last run is manageable.
runners_data.comment: Runs to a solid level at this distance and on good ground, going down by three lengths off a slightly higher mark at Doncaster last time. The question is whether he settles — he can be free-running and needs to relax to show his best.

runners_data.name: Mart
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's runner carries a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 — its natural home is at the rear of the field but the absence of any front-runner may see Taryn Langley (claiming 5lbs) find a forward position by default; form reads 475436 over six-furlong trips, shorter than this mile, and similar-going record (0W0P from 15) is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Running well below his best handicap mark and showing fair form in recent starts, he is versatile in terms of conditions and has experience at this distance. The form dipped last time at Newmarket, and whether 8f suits as well as shorter is worth bearing in mind.

runners_data.name: Campani
runners_data.note: David Simcock's four-year-old has genuine class credentials with two wins and four places from ten runs on similar going, and the form string 177-13 underlines the quality; Dougie Costello is a smart pilot but 50 days off the track introduces freshness risk, and though mapped to midfield the horse's profile means it could naturally push forward if the pace is truly missing.
runners_data.comment: Third here on his most recent outing, Campani has landed two races in recent starts and handles this track and today's conditions. He's capable when at his sharpest, and off a 50-day break, he rates as the one to beat on our figures.

runners_data.name: Luminous Warrior
runners_data.note: Another Dylan Cunha runner, this time ridden by Saffie Osborne, with a headgear entry (tongue-tie) and recent form of 700786 that reads poorly; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) notes displacement from its natural rear position, and similar-going form (0W1P from 15) offers little encouragement — the 12-day turnaround is short for a horse in this form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts but racing off a mark that continues to slide, he acts well at this distance on today's going and is fitted with a tongue-tie for the first time. Nothing more than a mid-division chance at best given the current run of form.

runners_data.name: Shaws Phoenix
runners_data.note: Carries cheekpieces and arrives from P Charalambous & J Clutterbuck's yard off 30 days, but a form string of 558-90 and the worst OR in the field (48) make this a difficult proposition; similar-going record of 0W2P from 15 runs confirms the horse rarely delivers on fast ground, and being pushed out of its natural hold-up position only compounds the challenge.
runners_data.comment: Tailed off at Wolverhampton on her most recent outing, she has questions to answer at this distance in particular and sits bottom of our rankings. The addition of first-time cheekpieces is a small hope, and she acts on any going, but it asks a lot.

runners_data.name: Sporty Socks
runners_data.note: William Stone's three-year-old is the youngest and lightest-weighted runner in the field (117lbs) and hasn't run for 65 days — the longest absence here — which is worth noting; form of 2653-7 includes a placed effort over 8f on Standard, and the horse shows 0W0P on similar going from 8 runs, though the drop in class relative to OR could offer some scope in a sprint finish.
runners_data.comment: Set too strong a pace and paid for it when well beaten here last time, she now returns from a 65-day absence with stamina over this distance still to fully prove. Some ability at 8f but needs to settle her running better to feature.

races.paceDynamic: With every single runner in this seven-horse field carrying a hold-up profile, there is no natural front-runner to set the gallop, meaning the early stages at Yarmouth's mile will almost certainly be a crawl as each rider waits for others to commit. The race will likely dawdle into the straight before erupting into a bunched sprint finish over the final two furlongs on going that the course reports confirm is Good to Firm, favouring quick acceleration rather than sustained galloping. Campani and Mart carry the highest ORs among the redistributed horses and, if any runner breaks from the group early, it is these two that have the profile — and trainer/jockey quality — to push forward and manufacture a lead in the absence of genuine pace. This race shape overwhelmingly favours runners with a sharp late burst and the ability to quickly find position in a compressed final-furlong sprint, meaning horses with clean form on good ground and strong closing kicks — rather than relentless gallopers — hold the clearest advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish From Bunch
scenarios.trigger: If the field idles through the early stages and the race becomes a dash over the final furlong on Good to Firm ground.
scenarios.body: If the field idles through the early stages and the race becomes a dash over the final furlong on Good to Firm ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Campani Dictates Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Campani or Mart breaks the deadlock and pushes forward to establish a solo lead from halfway.
scenarios.body: If Campani or Mart breaks the deadlock and pushes forward to establish a solo lead from halfway.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is artificially compressed so severely that only the sharpest finishers from the back of the group deliver a winning burst.
scenarios.body: If the pace is artificially compressed so severely that only the sharpest finishers from the back of the group deliver a winning burst.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one runner installs themselves at the head of affairs in the first two furlongs and is simply never challenged in the absence of any rival willing to go forward.
scenarios.body: If one runner installs themselves at the head of affairs in the first two furlongs and is simply never challenged in the absence of any rival willing to go forward.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Campani drifting in market with 50 days off the track — if money comes for this David Simcock runner it suggests stable confidence that the fresher horse is ready to dominate a field that offers no natural pace.

Monitor early race positioning closely: if Mart or Campani's jockeys push forward from the gate and find themselves alone on the lead, the entire race dynamic changes from sprint-finish to front-runner's race and all hold-up runners are immediately disadvantaged.

Sporty Socks has not run for 65 days — the longest layoff in the field — and William Stone's yard has recorded 0/5 over the last 14 days; fitness and stable form both require scrutiny before placing weight on this runner.

The going at Yarmouth is confirmed Good to Firm for the 4:50, slightly firmer than the stated Good, which slightly raises the premium on top-speed horses and could benefit Campani (1W4P sim-going) over rivals with poor records on fast ground such as Shaws Phoenix and Luminous Warrior.

Jockey quality is skewed towards the top of the market — Jack Mitchell, Dougie Costello and Saffie Osborne are all riding prominent yard runners; in a sprint finish where positioning in the final two furlongs matters enormously, the most experienced rider to find daylight first could prove decisive.

races.name: Branfords Handicap

runners_data.name: Giant
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Ian Williams, Ryan Kavanagh (5lb claimer) adds an ability handicap edge; four of last five runs on good ground produced a place finish (2nd, 3rd) suggesting the surface suits, though finishing position in today's pack will depend on how much of a run Dancing With Drums leaves.|
runners_data.comment: Second at Windsor last time, going down by just over two lengths off this very mark, Giant heads our figures in a nine-runner field and acts well across a range of trips. He is yet to win in recent starts but this is a fair opportunity.

runners_data.name: Wilde And Dandy
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride on this 147-day absentee, a lengthy break that is a genuine concern; placed at 7f on standard ground three times in recent history but the ring rustiness after nearly five months off makes it hard to trust at a key moment.|
runners_data.comment: Suited to today's trip and surface, he acts over 7-8f on a sound surface, but returns from a near five-month absence with his form having been below par before the layoff. Finding his feet on the comeback is the key question.

runners_data.name: Dion Baker
runners_data.note: Michael Wigham's yard in excellent current form (T14: 4/5) and this horse has won three of his last five starts including at this 7f Yarmouth trip on good ground — the most striking recent form in the race; his natural running style is hold-up but the congested rear means he is likely to race more prominently than usual, which is actually not a major inconvenience given his versatility and fitness (ran just two days ago).|
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last six starts and back just two days after landing at Brighton — the cheekpieces have clearly played their part. Our figures put him down the market, though an in-form yard and course/distance experience keep him of interest.

runners_data.name: Federal Envoy
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani partners this Charlie Clover runner who has struggled to translate his one placing on good ground into wins; a genuine hold-up horse who finds himself squeezed into a midfield slot by the weight of closers in this field, meaning he is unlikely to be in his comfort zone positionally.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up at Ripon last time, going down by a length off a 1lb lower mark, he acts at 7f and ranks third on our figures. He has shown his best to date on the all-weather, which adds a small question mark over today's turf conditions.

runners_data.name: Dancing With Drums
runners_data.note: The race-shaper and sole front-runner under Dougie Costello for trainer Adam Kirby; has form on good ground at 7f and 6f but a STYLE_FIT flag notes the prominent tag is already somewhat positional rather than natural — uncontested lead should still suit, though the absence of a recent win over 7f on genuinely good ground is a note of caution.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Kempton in May and is 1lb lower here than on his most recent outing, which is in his favour. Form has faded since that success though, and a bounce-back is needed over a trip that may stretch him slightly.

runners_data.name: Adelaide Bay
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's four-year-old has been running consistently at 7f on standard ground, placing once at Yarmouth in her last five; true hold-up horse whose five most recent runs are all on standard going rather than good, so the step up in ground condition is an unknown — mapped to midfield despite wanting to come from off the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up at Lingfield last time, going down by three lengths off a marginally higher mark, he now races below the level at which he has previously been successful, which gives him something to work with. Acts at 7f but his best form has come on the all-weather.

runners_data.name: Jungle Knight
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a win at 7f on soft for Mark Rimell but all five career starts have come on soft or standard ground — today's good-to-firm is his firmest test yet (headgear: tongue tie), and that going query is a genuine concern despite looking well positioned to track the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap here last time by a length, and drops in trip today which should be a positive. Effective on good ground and fitted with a tongue-tie for the first time, though 3lb higher than for that success is the key test.

runners_data.name: Hakin Adraar
runners_data.note: Martin Dunne's three-year-old has a thin recent form line on good going (2 runs, no wins or places) and is a true hold-up type shunted into a midfield role he will not naturally fill; Dylan Hogan rides but the combination of compromised position and patchy form at this level makes this one to monitor rather than rely upon.|
runners_data.comment: Last at Doncaster on his most recent outing in a clear step backwards, and his better efforts have tended to come on the all-weather. Has shown enough to suggest a revival is possible, but needs to bounce back quickly.

runners_data.name: Mayflower Rock
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's lightly-raced three-year-old carries the ⚠ fade flag and has never raced beyond 6f before, stepping up to 7f for the first time on good-to-firm ground — both the extra furlong and the firmer conditions are untested territory; Saffie Osborne rides but this is a significant ask for a horse with only three career runs.|
runners_data.comment: Finished last in a novice at Wolverhampton most recently, she sits at the foot of our figures in a nine-runner field with questions over trip and experience. The yard landed this race last year, which is of note, but she needs to bounce back significantly.

races.paceDynamic: Dancing With Drums is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival looking to contest the lead, Dougie Costello can dictate an uncontested, sustainable gallop from the front over this 7f Yarmouth straight. The Good To Firm conditions (confirmed by the going report for this 5:25 slot) will ensure a decent surface tempo but without pressure from behind, Dancing With Drums can control the fractions and keep the race honest rather than turning it into a sprint. The field is heavily stacked with hold-up types — Dion Baker, Hakin Adraar, Federal Envoy, Adelaide Bay, and Mayflower Rock are all true hold-up runners who have been mapped to midfield positions simply because the race shape cannot accommodate that many horses at the rear, meaning several will be racing out of their natural role. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-lead profiles who can track or make the running, with hold-up horses facing the twin handicap of a potentially modest pace and needing a strong final-furlong surge that a solo leader dictating can deny them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solo Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Dancing With Drums bowls along uncontested and sets a comfortable, unexposed tempo that the hold-up pack cannot reel in.
scenarios.body: If Dancing With Drums bowls along uncontested and sets a comfortable, unexposed tempo that the hold-up pack cannot reel in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough that horses tracking Dancing With Drums close up cruise into contention turning for home and overpower the leader.
scenarios.body: If the pace is honest enough that horses tracking Dancing With Drums close up cruise into contention turning for home and overpower the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces

scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Dancing With Drums burns too bright and the whole field bunches in the final two furlongs, turning the finish into a scrappy battle for position.
scenarios.body: If Dancing With Drums burns too bright and the whole field bunches in the final two furlongs, turning the finish into a scrappy battle for position.

watchPoints.text: Dancing With Drums sets every framing scenario — if Dougie Costello is crowded or bumped at the start and loses the lead to another runner, the entire race shape collapses and hold-up horses gain an unexpected advantage.

Dion Baker ran just two days ago (LR: 2d) and while the Wigham yard is red-hot, watch for signs of fatigue in the final furlong — if he fades having raced more prominently than ideal, it opens the race to true hold-up types behind him.

Jungle Knight has never encountered ground this quick (all prior runs on soft or standard) — if the good-to-firm surface inconveniences him, the main credible hold-up challenger to Dancing With Drums disappears from the equation.

Wilde And Dandy returns from 147 days off with Silvestre De Sousa booked — watch the market move; a well-backed absentee with a top jockey often signals stable confidence and could outrun the ring-rust concern if fit.

Multiple hold-up horses (Dion Baker, Hakin Adraar, Federal Envoy, Adelaide Bay, Mayflower Rock) will all be jostling for midfield positions on a straight 7f track — watch for potential traffic issues and interference in the closing stages as they all look for racing room simultaneously.
